principles: Host identity is declared metadata, not a CLI product enum.
Server policy and signed claims remain the authorization boundary.
Keep compatibility aliases only where they preserve existing behavior.
Change the smallest set of CLI surfaces that currently block real usage.
drivers: Developers must be able to reuse the same server-issued senior bundle across different agent hosts.
The CLI must not reject future hosts before the Authority Server can evaluate policy.
Existing codex, claude, fake, and Antigravity-adjacent behavior must not regress.

options.name: keep-closed-enum
cons: Blocks future and custom hosts locally
Forces repeated CLI releases for every new host name

options.name: free-declaration-with-compat-aliases
pros: Allows Codex CLI, Claude Code, Antigravity, and future hosts to declare themselves
Lets server policy produce the authoritative accept/reject result
cons: Requires tests to prove declaration does not imply authorization
May surface server rejection later instead of local enum rejection

options.name: server-issued-provider-list-cache
pros: Could validate against server policy earlier
Might improve diagnostics once policy discovery is stable
cons: Adds remote dependency and cache invalidation to a simple declaration path
Would optimize before fixing the real local correctness blocker

rationale: Choose free declaration with compatibility aliases because the correctness bug is local pre-policy rejection. The CLI should propagate declared host/provider metadata and leave authorization to the signed server claim path.

preMortem.scenario: Custom provider declaration is mistaken for authorization
preMortem.trigger: Code treats runnerProviderValid=true as sufficient proof of capability
preMortem.consequence: A self-declared host could appear trusted without server policy acceptance
preMortem.mitigation: Keep tests and code language explicit: declaration is metadata; API key, actor signature, lease, and server policy still gate claims.

preMortem.trigger: Changing provider type from closed union to string removes alias/default behavior
preMortem.consequence: Existing senior bundles and smoke tests fail
preMortem.mitigation: Preserve codex default and claude/claude_code alias normalization; update focused smoke assertions.

preMortem.scenario: Job create accepts arbitrary provider but server rejects with unclear diagnostics
preMortem.trigger: Command-catalog enum is relaxed but error reporting is not clear
preMortem.consequence: Developers think CLI is broken rather than server policy rejecting
preMortem.mitigation: Do not swallow server response; docs and readiness text explain that server policy rejection is authoritative.
